title: Cities: Skylines | Power, Politics, & Planning: Episode 3: Gentrification
premise: Donoteat01 argues new housing and downzoning fail incumbent renters in different ways, advocating incremental decommodification while acknowledging economic risks.
coverage: Full timestamped ASR and all49 original contact sheets/580 original indexed frames inspected, plus two inspected registered supplemental frames: Corbyn581 at1381s and unhappy-neighborhood582 at1112.8s. Total51 sheets/582 frames. Original sampling uses first available frame per5-second bin plus scene changes above0.3 at480px width. Six native-resolution targeted stills at300,1112.8,1125,1306.733,1381,1475.6seconds. QAPlanning identified the two brief supplemental moments between original samples. Complete assigned sample includes credits/token but may miss other brief inserts. Shared renderer derives FULL dialogue from every timestamped source word across chronological panel starts; authored JSON contains no dialogue excerpts or end times. Machine transcription/timing uncertainty remains. Empty sound arrays mean unannotated non-speech audio, NOT established silence; no dedicated soundtrack audition performed. Camera motion grounded in adjacent samples, not continuous video viewing. Supporting narrative/evidence: ../story-sheets/LdeirDrinWk.md; ../visual/LdeirDrinWk/index.json.

panels.heading: The game neighborhood visibly unhappy
panels.description: Many red frowning-face unhappiness icons float above row houses surrounding a cleared paved vacant lot beside the freeway. A red-frown location pin marks the lot; ordinary traffic and green-white streetcars remain visible.
panels.camera: Oblique gameplay view; a brief icon-filled moment identified around1112.53–1113.03. The single registered frame at1112.8 does not establish a pan or the icons' animation path.
panels.action: Game unhappiness indicators appear across nearby properties after the lot clearing. No individual tenant is tracked or observed being evicted.
panels.visualGag: Visual irony: the game itself supplies a chorus of unhappy faces just as the narration pivots to construction directly causing displacement, reversing the opening everyone-wins premise. These are observed game feedback icons; deliberate staging or comic intent is not established.
panels.notes: QAPlanning's additional brief-insert scan found the moment; independently inspected native evidence ../visual/LdeirDrinWk/targeted/at-1112.800s.png and registered frame582. Ordinary pedestrians/traffic later in this interval are not treated as a separate gag.
